audit_areas.assessment: One shared core, separate entry points and optional VM backend. Standalone has no VM dependency in its release build.
Existing owners, provisioning, API contracts, credential invalidation and resource observation retained. No second lifecycle manager introduced.
Exactly one existing workspace, no VM/disk provisioning or VM idle reclamation, Docker owns container resources and final lifetime.
Legacy effective defaults and aliases preserved; canonical defaults separated. Standalone rejects VM, roster, state and management fields.
Server retains schema3 identity/resource ownership and durable write protections. Standalone identity is read-only in memory; no account file.
Single-space paths still require credentials, current-identity checks, cookie/Origin/nonce protection; Server paths retained.
Shared managed startup and output decoding preserve VM behavior. Local payload identity, secret exclusion, cancellation and root control ownership remain explicit.
Same tasks, control lease, workers and UI. Lost local desktop owner blocks recreation; no duplicated task service or user-space picker.
Same tool and streaming semantics; paths adapted per target, DAV remains separately authenticated/listened. Local file payload runs as UID1001.
Server contains MSB; Workspace is a rootfs without MSB; Standalone reuses desktop dependencies and adds direct service. Independent deployment/build files are justified.
Target/source/image/cleanup gates retained. Mutable-tag race fixed by pinning launch references; historical reports are not rewritten.
Whole-service cold rollback is distinct from selected-workspace transfer. Source ownership retained; destination mapping explicit. Projected archival namespace now validated in dry-run and apply.
